stories.title: Macron's Paris Call: OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Mistral and 6 more AI firms sign a frontier-AI safety declaration; US, Google, Meta, China did not
stories.score_hints: Europe-first; fits 'AI rules' theme; 9 days after Merz sovereignty post, different topic

articles.title: AI firms sign Macron's Paris Call, but safety group says it lacks teeth
KI-Regulierung: Macron drängt auf internationale Sicherheitsstandards

facts.text: OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral are among ten AI companies that have signed a new declaration on the safety of advanced AI models, the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security.
It was agreed on Monday at a meeting hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron, on the opening day of the Paris Peace Forum.
Six countries signed: France, Canada, Finland, Norway, the Netherlands and Bahrain.
The other participating companies are Hugging Face, Cohere, Black Forest Labs, Domyn, Sakana AI and Synthesia.

Around 50 people joined by video, including OpenAI's Sam Altman, Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Microsoft president Brad Smith; US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent took part, but the US is not among the signatories. Google, Meta and China have not signed either.
Signatories committed to fail-safe mechanisms that can shut down their AI models, including during training and internal use, and to let qualified independent experts test them where appropriate.
Non-sensitive test results would be published in a common format, and governments and companies will share early warnings about serious incidents; whistleblowers get secure reporting channels.

French AI safety group CeSIA, which signed, says the text sets no common risk thresholds for deciding whether a model should be released and does not guarantee independent testers access; it wants governments to be able to suspend a model.
Macron compared untested AI to untested toys, arguing parents would not give a child an untested toy.

articles.title: Megaspeed imported $787m of Nvidia chips after the 2025 ban
Bericht: Jensen Huangs Affäre brachte Nvidia-Chips im Milliardenwert nach China
엔비디아, CEO 스캔들에 AI 투자 불안 겹쳐…이틀간 시총 627조 증발

facts.text: Nvidia says it banned all sales and shipments to Megaspeed in June 2025, and that the ban is still in place, a company spokesman told The Wall Street Journal.
Malaysian trade records show Megaspeed imported at least 17,544 Nvidia GB300 chips, worth about $787m, in November 2025, according to Bloomberg.

Megaspeed is a Singapore company; Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after Jensen Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive whom US officials believe to be a Chinese intelligence asset. China has denied the espionage claims.
Megaspeed has categorically denied the chip diversion allegations.

Senators Jim Banks (Republican) and Elizabeth Warren (Democrat) back a bill that would temporarily bar Nvidia from selling Chinese customers any chip more advanced than the H200; lawmakers are negotiating to add it to the annual defence bill.

The Information reported, citing two people who know Alice Huang, that she enabled shipments of Nvidia chips worth at least $7.5 billion to China, more than 240,000 A100, H100 and H200 systems, through a web of companies (per heise).
Three House committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed briefing on 18 November (TNW); heise reports he is due before a congressional committee next week.
Nvidia lost about $430 billion in market value over two days: shares fell 4.3% on the 9th and 5.47% on the 10th, about 9.5% in total, according to Reuters as cited by AI Times.
Microsoft overtook Nvidia as the world's second most valuable company, the first swap since June 2025; investors now watch Nvidia's earnings next week.

articles.title: 한국 디지털·AI 경쟁력, 세계 10위 도약...전년 대비 8단계 상승

facts.text: South Korea ranked 10th out of 70 countries in the 2026 World Digital and AI Competitiveness Ranking by Switzerland's IMD, up 8 places from last year, Korea's science ministry said on the 11th.
Korea placed 3rd in both 'technology infrastructure' (up from 7th) and 'efficiency' (up from 13th).
Four of the six new AI indicators ranked in the top 12, including the AI adoption index at 8th.
Weaker spots: companies' understanding of AI security risks (25th) and legislated AI policy (30th).
The US rose from 4th to 1st; Canada fell from 1st to 5th. In Asia-Pacific, Singapore was 2nd, China 7th and Japan 19th.
Korea ranked 1st in total R&D spending as a share of GDP and 8th in AI papers.
Governance rose from 34th to 27th; Korea ranked 1st on the new 'government core systems' index.

facts.text: Korea's government designated next-gen sensors, actuators and secondary batteries for humanoids as new tasks in its 'hyper-innovation economy' flagship projects, aiming to build a mass-production base by 2030.
The finance ministry discussed the plan at an emergency economic ministers' meeting on the 11th chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il; it adds 3 tasks to the existing 15.
Next-gen sensors centre on 'on-sensor AI' that senses and judges; next year 9 billion won goes to robotics, defence and mobility development and demos, 1.8 billion won to training experts.
For actuators (the parts that move a robot's arms, legs and fingers), next year 30 billion won goes to high-power, lightweight technology and about 3 billion won to humanoid demos.
The goal is to raise domestic share of core robot parts from 40% to 80%.

Medium-term budgets: 100 billion won for the K-robot ecosystem (2027-2029), 49.8 billion won for on-sensor AI chips (2027-2030), 271.4 billion won for battery competitiveness (2027-2031). (Convert to dollars at an article-given rate; article gives none, so check before writing.)

stories.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to everyone, with a /swarm multi-agent mode, at $2/$10 per million tokens
stories.score_hints: big model release; Korean accounts focused on Anthropic Fable 5.2 (trenddalkak 7.6x, 11-10), Gemini story not yet widely covered by them

facts.text: Google is making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers; it calls it its strongest model.
Two weeks ago Carbon was released to a set of cybersecurity defenders through Google's Fairwind Program.
Google says Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task than the next best external model.
Google is previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents that can be tracked in real time.
API price is the same introductory price as Gemini 4 Argon: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
It is rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
On the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark with Artificial Analysis, Carbon ranks #2 at more than 6X lower average cost per task than the top model.
A multi-agent Carbon team built an interactive 906K-triangle 3D reconstruction of Google's Platform 37 office from seven public planning PDFs, across 10 overnight loops.

stories.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: a humanoid sorts Mercedes-Benz car parts with a 96% success rate
stories.score_hints: physical AI with a European factory angle (Kecskemet, Sindelfingen)

facts.text: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, its most capable vision-language-action model to date.
In a proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, models helped Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate.
The pilots ran on active lines in Kecskemet, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany; the task is automotive kitting, sorting parts from bulk bins into trays in the order each vehicle needs.
The model was evaluated on over 200 distinct tasks, such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box and pipetting a liquid.
Inference-time reasoning guidance boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.
DeepMind also introduced a new benchmark for adversarial jailbreaks specific to robotics.
Gemini Robotics 2.5 is rolling out to Google's robotics partners.

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic face new oversight as New York's AI safety law takes effect

facts.text: New York opened a registration portal Tuesday; large frontier AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI must register by January 1, 2027.
The RAISE Act covers large frontier developers, defined as companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue.
They must publish safety frameworks on their websites, report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and issue public model transparency reports.
A new Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, and Trust (DIGIT) will implement the law.
Penalties can be as high as $1 million for one violation and $3 million for subsequent violations.
Governor Kathy Hochul also launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at Binghamton University, announced in January with $55 million in donations and capital.
